name: Catch Amazon resellers breaking your price policy with Bright Data, data tables and Telegram

parameters.content:
## Catch resellers undercutting your Amazon price policy

Your seller account shows your own offers. It does not show the other sellers who have listed themselves on your ASINs, and it does not show what they charge. This reads the public offer list instead.

### How it works

Put one row per product line in the `map_policy` data table: the search term buyers use, your brand name, the ASINs your floor covers, that floor price, and the sellers you have actually authorised. Data tables are built into n8n, so there is no spreadsheet to connect. Bright Data searches Amazon for each term and returns the full listing, including the other-seller offers.

**`Read Every Offer`** flattens the buy box and the offer array into one row per offer, then **`Find The Breaches`** keeps only the offers that are either from a seller not on your list or priced under your floor. Every breach carries the gap in currency and in percent.

There is no AI step. A breach is arithmetic, and a number is not a thing to have an opinion about.

### Setup

1. Bright Data, as a Header Auth credential. The free tier is 5,000 credits a month with no card.

2. A Data Table called `map_policy` with columns `keyword`, `brand`, `asins`, `map_price` and `authorized_sellers`, one row per product line, and a second called `map_breaches` with `checked_at`, `asin`, `title`, `seller`, `price`, `map_price`, `gap_percent`, `problem`, `on_buybox` and `url`.

3. A Telegram credential and your chat id in **Settings**.

4. Run it once with a real brand. A quiet day ends at **`Nothing To Report`** and sends nothing.

## 1. Your policy, not a guess
One row per product line: the search term, your brand, your floor price, and the sellers you have actually authorised.

## 2. One product line at a time
Each line gets its own search and its own limit, so a term Amazon chokes on costs that line rather than the whole run.

## 3. Ask Amazon, then wait
Keyword discovery took 30 seconds for six products when this was measured, so the job is started and polled rather than waited on.

## 4. Poll with a cap
`$runIndex` is the poll count. Without the cap a stuck snapshot would poll all night.

## 5. Every offer, not every product
The buy box is one offer among several. This flattens the offer array beside it, because the undercut is almost always the second seller.

## 6. Two tests, no model
Is this seller on your list, and is this price under your floor. An offer can fail both, and the alert says which.

## 7. A row each, one message
After the Split Out there is one item per breach, so the alert carries `executeOnce` - Telegram fed six items sends the same message six times.

## `number_of_sellers` is not a seller count

Measured 2026-08-30 across six rows: every one reported `number_of_sellers: 1`, and three of them carried an `other_sellers_prices` array listing two sellers. Filtering on that field would have reported a clean catalogue while a second seller was undercutting three ASINs.

The array is also null on rows that do have other sellers, so an absent array means the offer list was not returned, not that you are the only seller. Those ASINs are counted separately in the digest as unread rather than folded into the clean pile.

Both facts point the same way: count the offers you can see and say plainly how many you could not.
